mainTopic: Why כותש is not a listed מלאכה, and the rules of בורר on שבת
overview: The גמרא first explains why כותש (pounding) is not on the list of מלאכות, even though look-alike labors are listed. אביי says poor people skip pounding, so it is not an essential step. רבא's answer about the fixed number 39 is pushed off, and the גמרא settles on אביי. Next comes a ברייתא about בורר that seems to both allow and forbid selecting. עולא, רב חסדא, רב יוסף and רב המנונא each explain it, and each explanation is challenged. Finally אביי explains that selecting for immediate use is allowed, while selecting for later counts as storage, and רבא praises him. The גמרא then discusses sorting two kinds of food, where a basket or plate is פטור but a sieve or sifter is חייב. It brings רב דימי's story about רב ביבי's unsorted fruit basket, which proves nothing. Last comes חזקיה's ruling that sorting lupines from their waste is חייב. The גמרא says lupines are different, and the reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Even similar labors are counted
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: a labor is counted even though another labor resembles it, because it was done in the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is another labor that is similar to it, the משנה still counts it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to an earlier question: why does the משנה list labors like בורר, זורה and מרקד that look so alike?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle is that every separate labor done in the משכן gets its own place in the list. This is true even when it looks similar to another labor. This principle sets up the next question: if so, why is כותש not listed?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא דְּדָמְיָא לַהּ
phrases.english: even though there is one that is similar to it
phrases.notes: Refers to a labor that resembles another labor already on the list.

phrases.english: he counts it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא דְּדָמְיָא לַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle: every distinct labor done in the משכן is counted separately.
steps.terutzMaskana: Labors that look alike are still listed separately.

steps.title: Why is pounding not listed?
steps.stepSummary: If similar labors are counted anyway, the משנה should also list כותש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה also count pounding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list. Using the principle it just stated, it asks why כותש (pounding grain to remove its husk) is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pounding grain was also part of preparing bread. It is similar to דש, but the גמרא just said similar labors still get counted. So leaving it out needs an explanation.

phrases.english: Then let him also count pounding!

steps.kashyaTarget: The list of אבות מלאכות in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If similar labors are listed anyway, כותש should be listed too.

steps.title: אביי: poor people skip pounding
steps.stepSummary: כותש is not an essential stage of bread-making, since poor people bake without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because a poor person eats his bread without pounding the grain.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that pounding is not a necessary step in making bread, so it was not listed as its own labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The labors in the bread section are the steps that every bread-maker must do. A poor person grinds the grain with its bran and skips pounding, so pounding is only an optional extra.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
because a poor man eats his bread
without pounding.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the category: only essential stages are listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: כותש is optional, so it is not listed separately.

steps.title: רבא: the list is fixed at 39
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows רבי, who holds there are exactly 39 אבות מלאכות. Adding כותש would make 40.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי, who said the main labors are forty minus one. If he counted pounding, there would be forty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer: the number 39 is fixed, so the משנה could not add a 40th labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deal with whether pounding matters. He says the list is limited by the fixed number. This answer depends on the count, not on how bread is made.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi,
who said the primary labors
are forty less one,
and if he counted pounding
there would be forty.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא: the fixed count of 39 according to רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pounding could not be added without breaking the number 39.

steps.title: Swap one labor for pounding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה could have removed one similar labor and put כותש in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him take out one of those labors and put in pounding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer. Keeping the number at 39 does not explain why pounding in particular was left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only problem were the number, the משנה could drop one of the look-alike labors, such as בורר or זורה, and list כותש instead. So the count alone cannot be the real reason.

phrases.english: And let him take out one of these
and put in pounding!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that the count of 39 explains why כותש is missing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A swap keeps the count at 39, so the count does not explain choosing other labors over כותש.

steps.title: אביי's answer is the clear one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that אביי's explanation is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: the reason is like אביי said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבא's answer and settles on אביי's reason: pounding is not essential to making bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only אביי's answer explains why pounding in particular is left out. The fact that poor people skip it shows that it is not a basic stage of bread-making.
steps.whatToRemember: כותש is not listed because it is not a necessary step in making bread (אביי). The fixed count of 39 is not the reason.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: like Abaye.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's reason stands: pounding is not essential, so it is not listed.

steps.title: ברייתא on selecting foods
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person may select and eat or select and put aside, then says he may not select and is liable a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If there were types of food in front of him, he selects and eats, he selects and puts aside. And he may not select, and if he did select, he is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about בורר on שבת. It seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half allows selecting. The second half forbids it and even makes the person liable for a חטאת. The rest of the sugya tries to explain what each half is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: sin-offering, brought for an accidental Torah violation

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If there were types of food before him —
he selects and eats,
he selects and puts aside.
And he may not select,
and if he selected, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו מִינֵי אוֹכָלִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some selecting is allowed, and some selecting is a Torah-level violation.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can both allow and forbid selecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא contradicts itself and asks for an explanation. This question sets up the five answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looks like a simple question, but it is really pointing to a contradiction. The two halves must be about two different situations. Each אמורא will now suggest what those situations are.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does each half of the ברייתא refer to?

steps.title: עולא: today versus tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: עולא says selecting for use on שבת itself is allowed, but selecting for the next day makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, this is what it means: He selects and eats for that day, and selects and puts aside for that day. But for tomorrow he may not select, and if he did, he is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the first explanation. The difference is about when the food will be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selecting for שבת's own needs is allowed. Selecting for the next day is seen as real preparation work, which is a Torah violation.

phrases.english: Ulla said, this is what it is saying:
he selects and eats for that day,
and selects and puts aside for that day.
But for tomorrow he may not select,
and if he selected, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two halves are split by time: for שבת itself versus for tomorrow.

steps.title: רב חסדא: baking for today is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects that no מלאכה is allowed just because it is for שבת's needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: Is it allowed to bake for that day? Is it allowed to cook for that day?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks עולא's explanation by comparing בורר to other labors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking or cooking on שבת is forbidden even if you will eat the food on שבת. So בורר, which is also an אב מלאכה, should not become allowed just because it is for today.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda objected to it:
Is it permitted to bake for that day?
Is it permitted to cook for that day?

steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's split between today and tomorrow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other מלאכות are forbidden even for שבת's needs, so בורר should be the same.

steps.title: רב חסדא: less than the measure
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says selecting is allowed for less than a שיעור, but a full שיעור makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: He selects and eats less than the שיעור, and selects and puts aside less than the שיעור. But a full שיעור he may not select, and if he did, he is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a second explanation. The difference is about the amount being selected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability only starts at a set minimum amount, a כגרוגרת (dried-fig size). He suggests that a smaller amount is simply allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: less than the minimum amount for liability

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
he selects and eats less than the measure,
he selects and puts aside less than the measure.
But the full measure he may not select,
and if he selected, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two halves are split by amount: below the שיעור versus a full שיעור.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a small amount is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that doing a מלאכה on less than the שיעור is still forbidden from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Is it allowed to bake less than the שיעור?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב חסדא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below the שיעור a person is not liable, but he is still not allowed to do it in the first place. The ברייתא's words 'he selects and eats' sound fully permitted, so they cannot be describing a forbidden act.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to it:
Is it permitted to bake less than the measure?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's 'less than the שיעור' reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Less than a שיעור is still forbidden from the start, so it cannot be called permitted.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it depends on the tool
steps.stepSummary: Selecting by hand is allowed. With a basket or plate it is forbidden but not liable. With a sieve or sifter he is liable a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: He selects and eats by hand, and selects and puts aside by hand. With a קנון or a תמחוי he may not select, and if he did, he is exempt but it is forbidden. With a נפה or a כברה he may not select, and if he did, he is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a third explanation. The difference is about how the person selects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. By hand is not the normal way of working, so it is allowed. A sorting basket or plate is semi-professional, so it is rabbinically forbidden. A sieve or sifter is the real professional tool, so it is a Torah violation.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt from punishment but still forbidden

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
he selects and eats by hand,
he selects and puts aside by hand.
With a basket or a plate he may not select,
and if he selected, he is exempt but it is forbidden,
and with a sieve or a sifter he may not select,
and if he selected, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two halves are split by tool: by hand versus professional sorting tools.

steps.title: רב המנונא: the ברייתא never mentions tools
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא objects that the ברייתא says nothing about a basket or a plate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: Does it say anything about a קנון or a תמחוי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא attacks רב יוסף for adding details that are not in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good explanation should fit the words that are actually written. רב יוסף's reading depends on tools that the ברייתא never mentions.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna objected to it:
Does it teach anything about a basket and a plate?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מִידֵּי קָנוֹן וְתַמְחוּי קָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It adds details that are not in the text of the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב המנונא: food from waste versus waste from food
steps.stepSummary: Taking food out of the waste is allowed. Taking waste out of the food makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב המנונא said: He selects and eats food from the waste, and selects and puts aside food from the waste. Waste from food he may not select, and if he did, he is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives a fourth explanation. The difference is about what is being picked out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal way of sorting is to remove the waste and leave the good food. Picking out the good food instead is a change from the normal way, so it is allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Hamnuna said:
he selects and eats food from the waste,
he selects and puts aside food from the waste.
Waste from food he may not select,
and if he selected, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two halves are split by what is removed: food from waste versus waste from food.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא never mentions food from waste
steps.stepSummary: אביי makes the same complaint against רב המנונא: these details are not in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Does it say anything about food from the waste?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses רב המנונא's own type of objection against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food-from-waste is also a detail that is not written in the ברייתא. So רב המנונא's reading has the same weakness he found in רב יוסף's.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to it:
Does it teach anything about food from waste?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִידֵּי אוֹכֶל מִתּוֹךְ פְּסוֹלֶת קָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It adds a detail that is not in the text of the ברייתא.

steps.title: אביי: immediate use versus later
steps.stepSummary: Selecting for immediate use is allowed. Selecting for later in the day counts as selecting for storage, and he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: He selects and eats right away, and selects and puts aside for right away. For later that same day he may not select, and if he did, he is like one who selects for storage and is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a fifth explanation. It reads the words 'selects and eats' simply as 'selects in order to eat now'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selecting right before eating is just part of eating, not a work process. Selecting even for later on the same day is treated like preparing food for storage, which is the real מלאכה. This reading adds nothing that is not already in the words of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: like one who selects for storage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אביי with עולא. For עולא, 'that day' (לבו ביום) is allowed. For אביי, even later on the same day is forbidden. Only immediate use is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The פוסקים combine conditions from this sugya. Permitted selecting must be food from waste, by hand, and for immediate use.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
he selects and eats immediately,
and selects and puts aside for immediately,
but for later that day he may not select,
and if he selected, he is considered like one who selects for storage
and is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בּוֹרֵר וְאוֹכֵל לְאַלְתַּר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two halves are split by timing: immediate use versus later, which counts as storage.

steps.title: רבא praises אביי
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן told רבא about אביי's explanation, and רבא said that נחמני (אביי) spoke well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said it in front of רבא. He said to them: נחמני spoke well.
steps.whatsHappening: The sugya ends with רבא approving אביי's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reading is the only one that fits the plain words of the ברייתא without adding new details. רבא's praise makes it the accepted explanation.
steps.whatToRemember: The accepted rule is that בורר is allowed only for immediate use. Selecting for later, even on the same day, is like selecting for storage and makes him liable a חטאת.
steps.confusionAlert: נחמני is not a new person. It is a name רבא uses for אביי.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rava,
he said to them: Nachmani spoke well.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's 'immediate use' reading of the ברייתא is endorsed by רבא.

steps.title: Two kinds of food sorted: exempt or liable?
steps.stepSummary: A new case is presented: two kinds of food are mixed, and a person sorts some to eat now and some to set aside. רב אשי teaches פטור; רבי ירמיה מדיפתי teaches חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two kinds of food in front of him, and he sorted and ate, and he sorted and put aside: רב אשי teaches that he is exempt. רבי ירמיה מדיפתי teaches that he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case about two kinds of food mixed together. Two אמוראים report different versions of the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the cases were food mixed with waste. Here both items are food, and he sorts some to eat now and some to put down for later. One version says פטור and the other says חייב, so the גמרא will have to explain the disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Two kinds of food mixed together
He sorted and put it aside (for later)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean the act is fully permitted. Usually on שבת, פטור means there is no biblical liability, but the act may still be forbidden.

phrases.english: If there were two kinds of food in front of him,
and he sorted and ate,
and he sorted and put aside.
Rav Ashi teaches: exempt;
Rabbi Yirmeya from Difti teaches: liable.
phrases.notes: The two teach opposite versions of the same case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the conclusion of the food-and-waste discussion in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of two foods sorted and put aside, רב אשי says פטור and רבי ירמיה מדיפתי says חייב.

steps.title: How can רב אשי say exempt when the ruling says liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's version, because a teaching exists that says חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי teaches 'exempt'? But it is taught 'liable'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. There is a known teaching that says חייב, so how can he say פטור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions look like a direct contradiction about one case. If a ברייתא says חייב, רב אשי's version of פטור seems to go against it.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught (in a ברייתא)!

phrases.english: Rav Ashi teaches 'exempt'?
But it is taught 'liable'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's version from Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules חייב in this case, so a ruling of פטור seems to contradict it.

steps.title: Basket or plate versus sieve or sifter
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Sorting with a plain basket or plate is פטור. Sorting with a sieve or sifter is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is with a basket or a plate; that one is with a sieve or a sifter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two rulings deal with different tools, so they do not really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basket or plate is not a real sorting tool, so sorting with it is not the true מלאכה, and he is פטור. A sieve or sifter is a professional sorting tool, so using it is real בורר, and he is חייב. The tool decides whether the act counts as the actual מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. There is no contradiction
A basket and a plate (simple, non-professional tools)
A sieve and a sifter (real sorting tools)

steps.whatToRemember: Sorting with a real sorting tool (נפה וכברה) makes a person חייב. Sorting with ordinary utensils (קנון ותמחוי) is פטור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the way sorting is done, especially the tool used, helps decide whether it is the full מלאכה of בורר.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is with a basket or a plate,
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי's case: פטור.

phrases.english: that one is with a sieve or a sifter.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's case: חייב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 20 by splitting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (אוקימתא by tool)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: פטור applies when sorting with a basket or plate. חייב applies when sorting with a sieve or sifter.

steps.title: רב ביבי served an unsorted basket of fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that on רב ביבי's שבת, when רבי אמי and רבי אסי visited, רב ביבי put a basket of fruit in front of them without sorting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: It was רב ביבי's שבת, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי happened to come. He set before them a basket of fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי tells a story that might show something about sorting food on שבת. It sets up a possible proof that the next step will examine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי did not clean the fruit of its leaves and stems before serving. That might suggest he thought even taking food out of waste is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
It was the Shabbat of Rav Beivai,
phrases.notes: It was his turn to host and serve.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi happened to come,
he set before them a basket of fruit.
phrases.notes: The fruit was unsorted, still with its leaves and stems.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new report that might bear on whether taking food out of waste is allowed.
steps.raayaObject: Whether taking food out of waste (אוכל מתוך פסולת) is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ביבי's conduct of serving unsorted fruit

steps.title: The story proves nothing: maybe it was generosity
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says he does not know why רב ביבי did it. Maybe he held that sorting food from waste is forbidden, or maybe he wanted to look generous with a full basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I do not know whether it was because he held that taking food out of waste is forbidden, or whether he meant to show generosity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי himself admits the story is not a clear proof, because there are two possible reasons for רב ביבי's behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the fruit unsorted could be a halachic choice. It could also simply be hospitality, since a full, heaped basket tells guests to take as much as they want. Because either reason fits, nothing can be learned about בורר.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking food out of the waste

phrases.english: And I do not know
whether it was because he held
that taking food out of waste is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם עַיִן יָפָה הוּא דְּמִכַּוֵּין.
phrases.english: or whether he meant to show generosity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undoes the possible proof from Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects any halachic proof from רב ביבי's action
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The action can be explained by hospitality rather than halacha.

steps.title: חזקיה: sorting lupines from their waste makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה rules that one who sorts lupines (תורמוסים) out of their waste is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: One who sorts lupines out of their waste is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought from חזקיה about sorting lupines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising. Here the food is taken out of the waste, which רב המנונא (Step 15) treated as the allowed way to sort. Yet חזקיה says חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Lupines (a bitter bean that must be prepared before eating)

phrases.english: Ḥizkiya said:

phrases.aramaic: הַבּוֹרֵר תּוּרְמוֹסִים מִתּוֹךְ פְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁלָּהֶן — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: One who sorts lupines out of their waste is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling that seems to clash with the assumption, raised in Step 15 and in רב דימי's doubt (Step 23), that taking food out of waste is the lenient case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sorting lupines out of their waste is חייב.

steps.title: Does חזקיה forbid taking food out of waste?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that חזקיה must hold that even taking food out of waste is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that חזקיה holds that taking food out of waste is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to draw a general rule from חזקיה's ruling. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since חזקיה makes a person liable for taking lupines out of their waste, it seems he forbids all cases of food out of waste. That would go against the assumption behind רב המנונא's reading (Step 15) and רב דימי's story (Steps 22-23), where taking food out of waste is treated as the lighter case.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a proposed inference)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Ḥizkiya holds
that taking food out of waste is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broad conclusion from Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That חזקיה forbids taking food out of waste in general

steps.title: Lupines are a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference: lupines are different. The explanation continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lupines are different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says lupines are a special case, so no general rule can be learned. The reason comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה's ruling is limited to the unique nature of lupines. It does not mean he forbids all cases of taking food out of waste, so the general rule from earlier still stands.

phrases.english: Lupines are different
phrases.notes: The explanation of why continues in the next section.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning a general rule from the lupine case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Lupines have a unique feature that makes them an exception.
